summary: Validated the Sync Now fix (in-process background thread) end-to-end. Backend 4/4 pytest passed: POST /api/admin/sync/start returns 200 with {run_id, since, until, mode}; GET /api/admin/sync/runs/{run_id} transitions to 'done' within ~30s with all 9 progress keys (catalogs, users, templates, leads, lead_messages, wa_channels, wa_messages, contacts, open_activities); GET /api/admin/sync/status shows last_sync.finished_at + run_id; agent@homeivf.com correctly gets 403 on sync/start; migration/audit returns rows for every entity. Frontend E2E via Playwright: admin login → Admin → Migration tab → sync-card + sync-now-button rendered; click Sync Now → confirmation modal (Yes) → button switches to 'Sync in progress…', live progress panel shows Syncing… window, 'Sync started' info toast appears; sync completes to '✅ Sync #5 complete — 13 new, 148 updated' with per-entity deltas visible; Last Sync Run date updated to 09 Jul 2026 01:04 pm IST. Run Audit vs Odoo works and renders per-entity comparison table (26 rows) with 'Audit complete' toast. lead_chatter_messages shows tiny ~0.01% diff which is acceptable per spec (Odoo growing live). No 500s, no page errors, no console errors relevant to sync.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing live Odoo-synced data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Sync Now bug fix is validated. In-process threading works: run_id is created, progress updates, transitions to 'done', last_sync persisted, and 403 gating enforced for non-admins. UI flow (confirm modal → progress panel → toast → last sync date update) is intact. If retesting, note that concurrent sync attempts correctly return 409 — the test helper waits and retries.
rca of the issue: Original bug: /api/admin/sync/start relied on a detached subprocess writing to /var/log which is fragile in the managed container, so the button appeared to do nothing. Fix (already applied by main agent): sync_start now spawns threading.Thread → odoo_sync.run_sync(run_id, since, until) in-process, updates sync_runs progress + settings.last_sync via pymongo, and handles errors with a fallback finalizer. Verified working: 4/4 backend pytest + full UI e2e.
